transcript:
[00:00] Lena (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for making time today. I'm Lena from Redwood, AE on this account, and with me is Diego our solutions engineer and Sana from CSM. Quick sound check?
[00:08] Maya (Kairo): Sounds good, loud and clear. Maya here.
[00:11] Noah (Kairo): Noah, yep good.
[00:13] Evelyn (Kairo): Evelyn, hi.
[00:15] Diego (SE): Great. We'll keep this fairly informal, want to understand your stack and goals for quickstart and the free credits, time-to-first-token stuff, and then talk options hosted vs dedicated vs private.
[00:27] Maya: Perfect. To give context, Kairo is building a customer-support summarization feature that runs in-prod. We currently use a homegrown microservice on GKE with Triton for model serving, but ops cost is rising, and latency is kind of all over. We're considering moving to a managed API or reserved infra.
[00:45] Lena: Awesome, that's exactly what we help with. Quick qualifier: what's your expected QPS and tail latency SLO? and are you doing chat or single-turn generation?
[00:56] Maya: Mostly single-turn summarization, some multi-turn for follow-ups, expected steady-state 5 QPS with spikes to 40 QPS during peak biz hours. Latency SLO is 350 ms p95 if possible, but we'll degrade to 600 ms if need be.
[01:18] Noah: Important, we also have data residency for EU customers. Need to know if logs or prompt data leaves region.
[01:25] Lena: Good call. We have regional endpoints and options for Private (VPC) deployments. For hosted we provide regional hosting in EU and US; logs retention and audit-logging configurable. For Private you get customer-managed VPC and KMS/HSM integrations.
[01:42] Evelyn: Can you tell us about time-to-first-token with the PLG quickstart? How fast can our devs get a token and run an integration test?
[01:50] Diego: Typical dev flow: sign-up, get free credits, API key, and use the Quickstart SDK. Most teams hit first token in under 15 minutes, often 5-10 minutes if keys and environment are ready. We have a Quickstart repo and a one-click Postman collection.
[02:08] Maya: Nice. What are the free credits, any quota limits?
[02:12] Lena: We usually provide a trial credit pack (e.g., $500) for PLG signups; for sales-qualified leads we can apply a custom credit. Quotas are per-account but we can bump them for a PoC.
[02:23] Noah: Is there a self-serve flow for generating embeddings too, or just generation?
[02:28] Diego: All supported APIs are in the quickstart: text generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking. The SDK has examples for batching and async polling.
[02:35] Maya: Ok tell us about cost tradeoffs. Right now self-hosted is cheaper per token but ops overhead is high.
[02:42] Lena: Right — hosted is easiest for TTF token and minimal ops. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and cost per month with reserved GPUs — lower unit cost at scale. Private adds the enterprise security but typically higher setup fee. We can run a model recommendation to find cost break-even given your QPS and token usage.
[03:00] Evelyn: We saw mentions of quantization and batching in your docs. How much do those impact latency vs quality?
[03:06] Diego: Quantization tends to reduce memory and infer cost with small quality delta; depending on model family, 4-bit quant can be fine for summarization. Batching improves throughput but increases p95 latency, unless you use continuous batching or latency-aware schedulers. Our runtime supports smart batching and KV cache to balance that.
[03:26] Maya: When you say KV cache, are you referring to token caching across sessions? Could that help for repeated prompts?
[03:32] Diego: Yes — prefix and KV caching reduce recompute for repeated prefixes or long contexts. For summarization it's less impactful than for chat, but still helps for long documents.
[03:42] [00:03:45] Maya: Sorry, slight overlap: what's your typical model catalog for hosted? Are these open models or proprietary?
[03:50] Lena: We curate open models and Redwood-verified performance profiles; customers can pick model variants. We also support deploying customer-owned models in Dedicated/Private.
[03:58] Noah: For Private, what's the onboarding timeline? We need to plan for network teams and compliance reviews.
[04:04] Sana (CSM): For VPC/private we typically do a 6-8 week onboarding depending on approvals. That includes KMS/HSM setup, SOC2 paperwork, and network peering. Hosted is immediate and Dedicated ~2-4 weeks if you require reserved capacity and specific hardware.
[04:22] Evelyn: SOC2 — do you provide evidence and audit logs?
[04:25] Lena: Yes, we share SOC2 Type II reports, pen test summaries, and an audit log export. We'll share the security pack link in the follow-up.
[04:36] Noah: Who in Redwood will own the technical contact for our infra team?
[04:39] Lena: Diego will be main SE contact for benchmarks, and Sana will coordinate onboarding/CSM. I'm your AE for commercial coordination.
[04:47] Maya: Cool. I'm curious about fallback strategies. If hosted capacity hits a spike or region outage, what's the failover?
[04:54] Diego: We do smart routing — route by region, cost, latency, with automatic fallbacks to compatible model variants or other regions. For strict SLAs you can use Dedicated or Private. For hosted, we have soft-fallbacks and replication across regions for critical routes.
[05:10] Maya: Any gotchas with rate limits or throttling during spikes?
[05:14] Lena: We apply rate limits at account and route level; for PoC we can raise limits. Dedicated has predictable throughput not subject to multi-tenant throttles.
[05:23] Noah: Security question — how are keys managed for hosted? Do you support customer-managed KMS for keys at rest/encryption?
[05:31] Diego: Hosted uses our keys by default but you can opt into customer-managed KMS for Private; Dedicated can be configured as well. For hosted we encrypt data at rest and in transit, and PII redaction controls are available.
[05:43] Maya: Can we restrict token-level cost per route so product teams don't overrun budgets?
[05:48] Lena: Yes, Redwood Console provides per-route quotas, token-level cost breakdown, and alerts. You can configure guardrails for teams.
[05:57] [00:06:00] Evelyn: From a compliance perspective, do you support SSO/SAML and RBAC?
[06:02] Lena: Yes SSO, SAML, SCIM, and role-based access controls are supported. We'll share our SSO integration doc.
[06:12] Noah: About benchmarks — Diego, can you run a short local comparison with our representative prompt to show p95 on your hosted endpoint vs our Triton stack?
[06:19] Diego: Definitely. If you can provide sample prompts and expected QPS, we can run a hosted benchmark within a week and capture p50/p95/p99 and cost per token. I'll propose a benchmark plan after this call.
[06:31] Maya: Great, we have some redaction requirements — can Redwood support on-the-fly PII redaction or is that something we do pre-processing?
[06:38] Diego: We offer both: pre-processing libraries in the quickstart, and some guardrails in the pipeline. For regulated flows we recommend pre-processing plus private deployment.
[06:47] [00:07:00] Maya: On the PLG side, do you have sandbox environments for product teams to try without hitting production quotas?
[07:04] Lena: Yes, self-serve accounts get sandbox tokens and we can spin playground orgs. We also have templates for common quickstarts — summarization, semantic search, embeddings pipelines.
[07:14] Noah: Regarding model updates, can we pin model versions and do canary rollouts?
[07:19] Diego: Yes — model version pinning and rollouts (canary, A/B) are available in the Console. You can also set automatic fallback policies to previous versions.
[07:29] Evelyn: Cost again — is there a typical cost per 1k tokens on hosted for a moderate open model?
[07:35] Lena: It varies by model family—rough ballpark for a mid-sized open model is $0.50-$2 per 1k tokens on hosted. Dedicated reduces unit cost as you commit GPU hours. We'll include a tailored estimate after we see your token footprint.
[07:51] Maya: Ok. Another technical detail: how do you handle long context and memory? We sometimes process multi-document inputs >10k tokens.
[07:59] Diego: Our runtime supports long-context models and uses KV cache, and we optimize kernels based on sequence length. For very long contexts we recommend batching and using embeddings + retrieval augmentation for sections.
[08:13] Maya: Understood. If we do a PoC, what's a reasonable success criteria?
[08:18] Lena: Typical success criteria: meet p95 latency target (350-600ms), achieve cost per inference below X (we'll propose), and have stable integration in staging with RBAC and SSO working. Also business sign-off within 4-6 weeks for Dedicated discussions.
[08:34] Noah: Do you have references or case studies for customers that moved from Triton to Redwood?
[08:39] Lena: Yes we have a case study PDF; I'll include links in follow-up. A couple customers reduced ops headcount and improved p95.
[08:49] Maya: Can you walk briefly through a dev quickstart? I'm picturing my engineers copying a sample repo and running a test.
[08:56] Diego: Sure: 1) Sign up and get trial credits; 2) grab API key from Console; 3) clone quickstart repo; 4) run example to call /v1/generate with your prompt; 5) try embeddings. We have a Postman and Python SDK snippet. Most teams see first token in 5-15 minutes.
[09:18] [00:09:30] Maya: Ok perfect. Are there any known limitations for summarization models for hallucinations?
[09:36] Diego: Hallucination is model-dependent. We suggest prompt engineering and reranking, and Redwood Optimize recommendations for quantization and candidate reranking to reduce hallucinations. We also provide eval hooks for regression monitoring.
[09:50] Evelyn: What's the billing cadence? Monthly? Can we get consolidated billing across teams?
[09:54] Lena: Monthly billing, with invoicing for enterprise accounts. Consolidated billing is supported with org-level billing and per-team chargebacks.
[10:02] Maya: Great. Quick question: will trial credits allow burst testing to 40 QPS?
[10:07] Lena: Trial quotas are conservative but we can enable an elevated PoC quota for a short window to simulate spikes.
[10:13] Noah: Any pitfalls we've seen with customers doing a quick PoC?
[10:17] Diego: Mostly around realistic traffic shaping — sometimes teams test with tiny prompts and unrealistically high throughput; we recommend using production-like prompts for meaningful results. Also network peering and firewall rules can delay Private onboarding.
[10:32] Maya: Makes sense.
[10:35] [00:10:45] Lena: Alright, recap time. We'll: 1) Share pricing/credit details and security pack; 2) Diego will send benchmark plan and request sample prompts; 3) Kairo will share traffic pattern and sample dataset; 4) schedule SE deep dive next week. Anything to add?
[10:56] Maya: Please include the Quickstart repo link in the email.
[10:59] Lena: Will do. We'll also include the Postman collection and SSO docs.
[11:04] Evelyn: Can we get a high-level estimate for Dedicated hardware — e.g., one A100 pool vs shared?
[11:09] Lena: I'll include a Dedicated sizing stub in the follow-up; we'll need expected concurrency and model size to be precise.
[11:16] Noah: Ok. One last security ask: we need to review your pen test report before we give access to any EU PII.
[11:23] Sana: Noted — we'll attach the pen test summary and SOC2 in the follow-up link.
[11:28] [00:11:50] Maya: Thanks everyone. That was helpful.
[11:31] Lena: Thanks all — we'll follow up today with artifacts.
[11:34] Diego: Thanks, bye.
[11:36] [End of transcript]
